annotations.description: Casting Shardless Agent before combat is suboptimal when Subtlety (a 3/3 flyer) could attack first. Additionally, casting Shardless Agent before activating Windswept Heath means the cascade could hit cards that would be better drawn naturally. More importantly, the player has Birthing Ritual on the battlefield which triggers at end step - having both Subtlety and Shardless Agent gives a sacrifice target, but sequencing matters. The main issue is casting a creature before combat when there's no reason to - Subtlety could attack into the opponent's tapped-out board (both lands tapped, Bowmasters and Orc Army are summoning sick). Attacking with Subtlety for 3 flying damage first, then casting Shardless Agent in second main would be strictly better.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Shardless Agent in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Subtlety first (3 flying damage with no possible blocks since opponent's creatures have summoning sickness), then cast Shardless Agent in post-combat main phase to avoid giving information before combat.

annotations.description: The opponent's hand contains Dismember, Flare of Denial, Abhorrent Oculus, and Force of Negation. Force of Negation only counters noncreature spells, which is less relevant against MiniMx's hand of creatures (Phelia, Flickerwisp, Overlord of the Balemurk). Flare of Denial counters ANY spell and can be cast for free by sacrificing a nontoken blue creature (the opponent controls Subtlety, a blue creature). This makes Flare of Denial a much more dangerous card to leave in the opponent's hand, as it can counter MiniMx's creature spells for free. Abhorrent Oculus is also a consideration as a 5/5 flyer that generates card advantage, but the opponent needs 6 cards in graveyard (they have 6 exactly) and 3 mana (they have access to it). However, Flare of Denial's ability to freely counter any spell — including the Overlord of the Balemurk or Phelia that MiniMx wants to deploy — makes it arguably the most impactful card to take.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to discard Force of Negation, which only counters noncreature spells
annotations.betterLine: Take Flare of Denial, which counters any spell and can be cast for free by sacrificing Subtlety (a nontoken blue creature already on the battlefield). This is more threatening against MiniMx's hand full of creatures. Alternatively, taking Abhorrent Oculus (opponent has exactly 6 cards in graveyard to cast it) removes a huge threat.

annotations.description: MiniMx Folksy has a 4/4 Orc Army Token and a 1/1 Orcish Bowmasters available to attack. The opponent's only creature is Subtlety (3/3 flying) which is TAPPED and therefore cannot block. This means both creatures could attack unimpeded for 5 damage, bringing the opponent from 13 to 8 life. With Overlord of the Balemurk ticking down and aggressive creatures on board, pushing damage is important. The reasoning about Subtlety blocking is incorrect since it's tapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to attack with any creatures
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Orcish Bowmasters and Orc Army Token for 5 unblocked damage (opponent's only creature Subtlety is tapped). This represents significant free damage with no risk.

annotations.description: MiniMx Folksy cast Dismember (likely paying life for Phyrexian mana) and KimiK2 Philo is choosing the target for their opponent's Dismember. They targeted their own Abhorrent Oculus (a 5/5 flyer that generates manifest dread tokens every opponent's upkeep) instead of a less valuable creature. The reasoning mentions wanting to target Overlord of the Balemurk but the actual choice was Abhorrent Oculus. Abhorrent Oculus is by far the most powerful creature on KimiK2's board - it's a 5/5 flyer with an incredibly powerful recurring ability. Subtlety is a 3/3 flyer that has already used its ETB trigger. Losing the Oculus is devastating compared to losing Subtlety.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Abhorrent Oculus as the target for opponent's Dismember, destroying their best creature.
annotations.betterLine: Should have chosen Subtlety as the Dismember target since it's a less valuable creature (3/3 flyer with already-used ETB) compared to the Abhorrent Oculus (5/5 flyer with recurring manifest dread value engine). Alternatively, could have countered Dismember with Flare of Denial by sacrificing a blue creature.

annotations.description: Playing Shadowy Backstreet instead of Marsh Flats means the land enters tapped, leaving MiniMx unable to use that mana this turn. Marsh Flats would enter untapped and could be cracked immediately to fetch an untapped land (like a Plains or Swamp), providing an additional mana source this turn. With Phelia summoning sick and Flickerwisp in hand (costing 1WW), having access to more untapped mana next turn or this turn is important. Additionally, Marsh Flats could fetch a Plains to ensure Bleachbone Verge is fully online. The surveil 1 from Shadowy Backstreet is marginal value compared to the tempo loss of a tapped land, especially when behind on board against a Subtlety.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Shadowy Backstreet (enters tapped) as the land for turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Marsh Flats instead, which enters untapped and can be cracked to fetch an untapped land, providing more mana flexibility this turn and next turn for casting Flickerwisp or other plays.

annotations.description: Playing Plains instead of Marsh Flats is slightly suboptimal. Marsh Flats can fetch a Plains (or Swamp) and thin the deck, plus it fills the graveyard which matters for potential future Overlord of the Balemurk triggers. Additionally, having Marsh Flats on the battlefield gives flexibility to crack it at instant speed later. The player already has white mana available from Bleachbone Verge (with Godless Shrine providing the Swamp/Plains type), so playing Marsh Flats and cracking it would accomplish the same mana development while providing deck thinning and graveyard fuel.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Plains from hand as their land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Marsh Flats instead, which can be cracked to fetch a Plains while thinning the deck and adding a card to the graveyard for synergy with Overlord of the Balemurk's mill/recursion ability.

annotations.description: Subtlety is tapped and cannot block, so both Orcish Bowmasters and Phelia could attack freely for 3 damage (putting opponent to 5). Additionally, Phelia's attack trigger could exile one of the opponent's two Birthing Rituals (which are generating massive value), getting a +1/+1 counter when it returns. The stated reasoning that 'Subtlety can block Phelia' is factually wrong since Subtlety is tapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to attack with any creatures
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Orcish Bowmasters and Phelia. Use Phelia's trigger to exile a Birthing Ritual (or Subtlety to remove a blocker permanently). Deal 3 unblocked damage, putting opponent to 5 life with strong board pressure.

annotations.description: Failed to play Marsh Flats before casting Flickerwisp. Playing lands before spells is fundamental sequencing - it preserves information advantage, provides additional mana options, and costs nothing. The land drop should always happen first unless there's a specific reason not to.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Flickerwisp without first playing Marsh Flats from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Marsh Flats first (don't need to crack it yet), then cast Flickerwisp. This preserves the option to crack Marsh Flats later if needed for additional mana or deck thinning.

annotations.description: Targeted opponent's Birthing Ritual with Phelia, which only temporarily exiles it (returns at end step) and doesn't give Phelia a +1/+1 counter since it's not under MiniMx's control. Flickering their own Flickerwisp would have given Phelia a +1/+1 counter AND generated another Flickerwisp ETB trigger to exile an opponent's permanent (like a Birthing Ritual) more effectively.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted opponent's Birthing Ritual with Phelia's exile trigger
annotations.betterLine: Target own Flickerwisp - Phelia gets a +1/+1 counter, and when Flickerwisp returns at end step, its ETB can exile a Birthing Ritual or other key permanent. Alternatively, target own Orcish Bowmasters for a counter on Phelia plus another ping and amass trigger.

annotations.description: At 4 life facing a 3/3 flying Subtlety that threatens lethal, returning Solitude to hand would provide a hard removal answer that also gains life via lifelink. While Solitude can't be cast this turn (only 3 untapped mana vs 3WW cost), it could be cast next turn to permanently exile Subtlety and gain crucial life. Emperor of Bones is immediately castable but doesn't address the lethal flying threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Returned Emperor of Bones from graveyard to hand
annotations.betterLine: Return Solitude to hand as the best answer to Subtlety, which threatens lethal in the air. Solitude could be cast next turn to exile Subtlety and gain 3 life, stabilizing a precarious position at 4 life.
